title: Faith Explorer
description: Eight equal-sized, alphabetically ordered tiles for faith traditions of South Asia (Buddhism, Christianity, Hinduism, Islam, Jainism, Sikhism, Jewish communities and Zoroastrians (Parsis)). Learners choose a faith and one of five lenses (Origins, Sacred texts, Place of worship, A major festival, A core idea) to read a short card in followers' own terms, and use Compare mode to see two faiths side by side through the same lens, without ranking.
creator: Aaryav Sharma
subject: South Asian cultures
World religions
South Asia
Religious pluralism
Comparative study of religion
publisher: Roots & Rivers: An Interactive Guide to South Asian Cultures for High School Students
audience: Students, Educators, South Asian student club leaders
learningObjectives: Compare South Asian faith traditions on the same five dimensions: origins, sacred texts, place of worship, a major festival and a core idea.
Describe each faith in the terms its followers use, without ranking.
Identify similarities and differences between two faiths through a single lens.
prerequisites: Chapter 3: Empires and Encounters (early Islam in South Asia, the Bhakti movement, Sufism and Guru Nanak)
Willingness to describe beliefs neutrally, in followers' own terms
keyQuestions: Where did each faith begin, and what texts does it treasure?
How are two faiths alike and different when viewed through the same lens?
Why does fair comparison mean describing, not ranking?
misconceptions: Sikhism is a mix of Hinduism and Islam.
controls: Lens menu (Origins, Sacred texts, Place of worship, A major festival, A core idea)
Click or tap a faith tile
dataSources: The Pluralism Project, Harvard University (Hinduism, Sikhism): https://pluralism.org/
UNESCO World Heritage Centre (Lumbini, Mahabodhi Temple, Churches and Convents of Goa): https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/
Pew Research Center, Religion in India: Tolerance and Segregation (2021): https://www.pewresearch.org/religion/2021/06/29/religion-in-india-tolerance-and-segregation/
Card facts checked against the sources listed in the Chapter 5 fact log (Guru Granth Sahib, Khalsa, Jainism, Mahavira, Paradesi Synagogue, Parsis, Iranshah Atash Behram and others)
